title: The INDEX function: the value at a position
summary: INDEX returns the value at a given row and column inside a range.
intro: `INDEX` returns what is in a given cell of a range: the second row, or the third row and second column. It becomes very powerful with `MATCH`, which gives it the row number.
args: The row number inside the range.
The column number inside the range, if it has more than one column.
examples: The second item in the names column.
The third row and third column of the table.
With `MATCH`: the price of "Pen", wherever it is.
errors: The row or column number is outside the range.

faq.a: Because `MATCH` finds the row number and `INDEX` returns the value from it, so you can search any column and return from any column.
